Hello Kitty toaster

A two-slice Sanyo toaster in pale pink, with Hello Kitty’s face and a script logo on its side: a kitchen appliance turned into character goods.

Source
V&A: Toaster, showing Hello Kitty, FE.21-2015
Creator
Sanyo Denki (manufacturer); Hello Kitty character by Sanrio
Made
1998
Style
Kawaii (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Cute, sweet, gentle
Evidence
Inspected the V&A photograph 2015HW1063 of object FE.21-2015 (1200 × 900 px, IIIF) in a scratchpad copy. Not stored.
Reviewed
2 October 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

The V&A describes the toaster as “plastic and metal; electrical components, manufactured by Sanyo Denki, Japan, 1998”, and acquired it with a Hello Kitty kettle and rice cooker in 2015. V&A FE.21-2015.

The museum calls Hello Kitty “the ultimate symbol of Japanese cute”, launched by Sanrio in 1974 for pre-adolescent girls and later used on domestic appliances such as kettles, toasters, and rice cookers. V&A FE.21-2015.

Observed

  • The body is a rounded box in pale, slightly glossy pink, with a chrome top around two bread slots.
  • On the side, a Kitty head in white with a hot-pink fuzzy outline, a pink flower at one ear, black dot eyes, whiskers, and a yellow nose, sits under the words “Hello Kitty” in a pink script.
  • The base is three stacked bands of a stronger pink with rounded ends; the lever and the browning knob are pink too.
  • The Sanyo name is printed small and pale below the face. There are no other markings.

Why it belongs

The toaster shows kawaii as a surface applied to an ordinary product: the form stays a standard toaster, and color plus one small character face carry the style.

Pink is used in two tones, pale for the body and stronger for the base and controls, so the object stays soft without becoming one flat color.

Borrow

Put one small character face on a large plain pastel surface, with the name in a rounded script above it.

Use a pale tint for the main surface and a stronger tint of the same hue for controls and edges.
